Implemented bounds-safe SysV DT_HASH handling in `PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup` and `PackLinuxElf64::elf_lookup` (`src/p_lx_elf.cpp`) to prevent heap OOB reads when walking DT_HASH chains.

Key changes (minimal, non-test files only):
- Read `n_chain` from `hashtab[1]` (SysV hash header).
- Removed unconditional use of `chains[si]`.
- Compute a safe `chain_limit` using the known end of the DT_HASH table (`hashend`), or best-effort fallbacks (`l_hash` or EOF).
- Only traverse the chain when `n_bucket && chain_limit`.
- During traversal, stop safely if the symbol index would exceed `chain_limit`/`symnum_max` or if dynsym bounds are suspicious.

Verification:
- `secb build` succeeds.
- `secb repro` no longer triggers AddressSanitizer; the PoC now terminates with `NotPackedException: not packed by UPX` (expected for the provided testcase) and no sanitizer errors.

Diff summary:
- Modified `src/p_lx_elf.cpp` in both 32-bit and 64-bit `elf_lookup` implementations with the above guard logic.

While walking ELF DT_HASH chains to resolve symbols the code can index past the end of the chains table and invoke a 32-bit read (via the get32/get_le32 path), causing a 4-byte heap OOB read. A malformed or malicious DT_HASH can therefore trigger crashes and potential information disclosure.

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/upx/build/debug/upx -l /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/upx

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/upx/build/debug/upx -l /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/upx

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup (src/p_lx_elf.cpp).     if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

<issue_description>
Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup (src/p_lx_elf.cpp). While walking ELF DT_HASH chains to resolve symbols the code can index past the end of the chains table and invoke a 32-bit read (via the get32/get_le32 path), causing a 4-byte heap OOB read. A malformed or malicious DT_HASH can therefore trigger crashes and potential information disclosure.

    fi

    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."

    if /usr/local/bin/compile \

<issue_description>
Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup (src/p_lx_elf.cpp). While walking ELF DT_HASH chains to resolve symbols the code can index past the end of the chains table and invoke a 32-bit read (via the get32/get_le32 path), causing a 4-byte heap OOB read. A malformed or malicious DT_HASH can therefore trigger crashes and potential information disclosure.

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then

        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi

else

fi

<issue_description>
Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup (src/p_lx_elf.cpp). While walking ELF DT_HASH chains to resolve symbols the code can index past the end of the chains table and invoke a 32-bit read (via the get32/get_le32 path), causing a 4-byte heap OOB read. A malformed or malicious DT_HASH can therefore trigger crashes and potential information disclosure.

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \

        exit 1
    fi

        exit 1
    fi

    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \

        exit 1
    fi

        exit 1
    fi

else

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \

        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi

    esac
else

    exit 1
fi

    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

        git submodule update --init --recursive

    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

        else

    fi

    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

Implemented bounds-safe SysV DT_HASH handling in `PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup` and `PackLinuxElf64::elf_lookup` (`src/p_lx_elf.cpp`) to prevent heap OOB reads when walking DT_HASH chains.

- Removed unconditional use of `chains[si]`.
- Compute a safe `chain_limit` using the known end of the DT_HASH table (`hashend`), or best-effort fallbacks (`l_hash` or EOF).
- Only traverse the chain when `n_bucket && chain_limit`.
- During traversal, stop safely if the symbol index would exceed `chain_limit`/`symnum_max` or if dynsym bounds are suspicious.
